name: PR and media agencies
shape_facts: Services: press relations, media buying, events, influencer relations, crisis communications, corporate comms
Number of retainer clients and typical sectors (government, real estate, FMCG, tech, hospitality)
Team size and roles (account managers, writers, media relations, event staff)
Whether they buy media space on behalf of clients and handle the money
Languages and markets covered (Urdu/English press, Arabic/English, Canadian outlets)
How media contacts, coverage and client reporting are kept today
Use of monitoring tools or manual clipping
scope_rule: pi notes how the agency operates: media list management, coverage tracking, client reporting, approvals, event logistics, media-buying billing, collections, capacity and new business. pi gives no legal, defamation, regulatory or crisis-strategy advice, and does not take journalists’ or clients’ personal contact details, client confidential information, or staff personal data. It records roles and outlet types only. Requests to plant false stories, pay for undisclosed coverage where unlawful, smear competitors, fake reviews or bribe officials are declined.

vocabulary.Media list: contacts at publications and channels for pitching
vocabulary.Coverage / clippings: articles and broadcasts that resulted from PR work
vocabulary.Embargo: news held until an agreed release time
vocabulary.Press kit: package of releases, photos and facts for journalists
vocabulary.Media buying: purchasing ad space or airtime for clients
vocabulary.Seeding: sending products to influencers or media
vocabulary.Wrap-up report: summary of coverage after a campaign

problems.phrase: Our media list is out of date and journalists keep changing outlets
Each account manager keeps their own contacts in their phone
When someone leaves, their media relationships go with them
Clients ask for coverage reports and we spend days compiling clippings
We can’t show clients the value of coverage in a way they accept
Press releases go through six rounds of client approval
News goes stale because approval came too late
We pay newspapers for ads and the client pays us months later
Media buying commissions and rebates are hard to reconcile
Retainer clients expect unlimited events and crisis support
Event suppliers deliver late or the wrong setup
Event budgets overrun and we absorb it
We miss mentions of clients because monitoring is manual
Coverage gets mixed up between clients in our records
Clients leave after a year saying they didn’t see impact
Pitches for new accounts take weeks and win rate is low
Our own visibility is poor, ironic for a PR firm
Weekend crises land on me personally, no rota
Influencer seeding products go missing or aren’t tracked
Media regulator or permit paperwork for events is chaos
Team uses three different templates for releases
Junior writers’ drafts need heavy rewriting
I can’t see which client the team spent the week on

seasons: - Pakistan: budget announcement (June), Independence Day, Ramadan and Eid campaigns, PSL season, wedding and lifestyle season in winter; elections bring sharp spikes in media demand and cost. - UAE: GITEX, Dubai Shopping Festival, Arab Health, Cityscape, National Day, Ramadan and Eid; summer is slower with many journalists travelling. - Canada: autumn and spring announcement windows, holiday gift guides (October–November), summer slowdown. - Year-end award seasons and annual reports create corporate comms peaks.
care: No legal, defamation, regulatory or crisis-response advice; if a crisis is live, note the operational problem only.
Do not take journalists’ personal numbers, client confidential plans or unannounced news.
Decline fake news, smear campaigns, fake reviews, undisclosed paid coverage where unlawful, or bribing officials.
If a crisis involves danger to people (accident, threat), pi points to emergency services first.
Political or sensitive content: stay neutral, note only the operational problem.
Client names are not recorded; use sector descriptors.
build_ideas: Shared media contact register owned by the agency (outlet, role, beat, last contact), with access controls
Pitch and story tracker per client: angle, outlets pitched, responses, coverage achieved
Coverage log with links, screenshots and outlet type, feeding an automatic monthly client report
Approval workflow for releases with timestamps and automated client nudges
Media-buying ledger per client: bookings, outlet invoices, client billing and payment status
Event planner: supplier list, deliverables, deadlines, budget versus actual
Seeding tracker for products sent to influencers and media, with follow-up dates
Out-of-hours rota for crisis monitoring with escalation chain
Retainer scope tracker comparing agreed activities against delivered work
New business pipeline with stage and follow-ups
Owner dashboard: active clients, coverage this month, pending approvals, receivables, team load

exchange.text: We spend the first week of every month just compiling coverage reports for clients.
That’s a big chunk of the month going into compiling rather than doing PR — noted. How does the team find and collect the coverage today?
Google alerts, people sending screenshots, and someone checks the papers.
Noted, a mix of alerts, screenshots and manual checking. Do clients ever say a piece is missing from their report?
Yes, and sometimes we put one client’s clipping in another’s report.
Understood, missing clippings and mix-ups between clients — both noted. How many retainer clients are you reporting to each month?
